detail.title: Epistemic Justice and Foundational Assumptions in AI Metareasoning
detail.summary: AI metareasoning frameworks benefit from integrating epistemic justice to recognize community expertise and ethics-based auditing to structure validation of automated outcomes. New evidence suggests that metareasoning processes, particularly when handling model misspecification, are subject to path-dependent inferential errors. Effective augmentation requires maintaining cognitive flow, which necessitates that systems adapt interventions to the user's current contextual state while remaining aware of inherent path-dependency risks in belief updating.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating path-dependency findings from preference research into meta-reasoning frameworks.

detail.title: Synthesis of Meta-Reasoning and Preference Formation Insights
detail.summary: This cycle integrates findings from path-dependent belief updating into meta-reasoning frameworks. Evaluation of foundational assumptions now incorporates evidence on how misspecified model regimes generate non-systematic preference structures, advancing the governance of automated metareasoning.
